title: Cyber Warfare Technician
raw_text:
8-170A. Military Occupational Specialty 170A-- Cyber Warfare Technician (Effective
202507)
a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
b. Prerequisites. DA Pam 611-21.
c. MOS 170A. MOS 170A is an accession MOS. The preferred CMF feeders are the 17, 25, and
35 Series MOSs, however, all other enlisted MOSs that demonstrate a strong technical
background to include documented operational experience and education may apply. Applicants
from other military services (Air Force, Marine Corps, and Navy) who can substantiate their
qualifications with performance evaluations, awards, and certificates are encouraged to apply for
MOS 170A. The proponent sets and maintains the technical qualifications for the MOS. Please
refer to https://recruiting.army.mil/ISO/AWOR/170A for current selection criteria and proponent
contact information. The Warrant Officer accessions process is available at
https://recruiting.army.mil/ISO/AWOR; please direct any accessions related questions to the
Warrant Officer Recruiting Branch at woteam@usarec.army.mil.
d. Associated SQI.
    (1) 0--No special qualifications.
    (2) 8--Instructor.
    (3) P--Parachutist.
    (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
    (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
e. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 for (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
Warrant Officer MOS).
f. Qualifications.
    (1) WO1/CW2 must--
         (a) Complete the Cyber Warfare Technician Warrant Officer Basic Course.
         (b) Be a U.S. citizen.
         (c) Obtain a fully adjudicated TOP SECRET clearance with eligibility for access to
sensitive compartmented information (SCI), prior to Warrant Officer Candidate School attendance
         (d) Soldier must be capable of passing a counterintelligence scope polygraph (CSP) to
hold the MOS. Soldiers who refuse to take or fail a CSP will be reclassified.

        (e) Formal Training (successful completion of 170A Cyber Warfare Technician Warrant
Officer Basic Course conducted under the auspices of the US Army Cyber School) is mandatory.
Waiver may be granted by Commandant, US Army Cyber School, Fort Eisenhower, GA 30905-
5300.
        (f) Upon completion of 170A Cyber Warfare Technician Warrant Officer Basic Course,
WO1s incur a 6 year term of service obligation.
   (2) CW3 must—
         (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (1).
         (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Advance Course (WOAC) for CW2(P) and CW3.
   (3) CW4 must--
         (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (2).
         (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Intermediate Level Education (WOILE) for CW3(P) and
CW4.
   (4) CW5 must—
         (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (3).
         (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Senior Service Education (WOSSE).
g. Duties.
   (1) WO1/CW2 must-
        (a) Manage operational teams in support of offensive and defensive cyberspace
operations.
        (b) Plan, administer, manage, maintain, and integrate actions in support of offensive and
defensive cyberspace operations.
        (c) Establish priorities and provide guidance for collection, exploitation, analysis and
reporting missions.
        (d) Direct network terrain audits, digital forensics processes, and exploitation missions.
          (e) Advise and assist commanders and staffs in formulating plans for cyber operations.
         (f). Mentor, train, and coach Soldiers and leaders on the technical and tactical aspects of
cyberspace operations.
         (g) Execute defensive cyberspace operational tasks at the senior level to identify, locate,
isolate, and mitigate cyberspace threats within the DODIN.
         (h) Execute offensive cyberspace operational tasks at the senior level to prepare the
operational environment, gain access, establish persistence, and deliver effects against targeted
systems or infrastructure.
         (i) Inform individual training requirements for cyberspace certification.
(j) Provide updates to unit level standard operating procedures.           (2) CW3 must--
         (a) Perform duties described in paragraph g (1).
         (b) Validate architectural analysis, administer penetration testing, and coordinate response
actions.
         (c) Manage the execution of Cyberspace Defense; Cyber Effects Enabling Activity, and
Cyberspace Effects Operations actions.
         (d) Monitor cyberspace operations to ensure mission execution is within authority
guidelines and operational risk tolerances.
         (e) Provide post-incident analytic input and mitigation recommendations as necessary.
          (f) Validate individual and collective training requirements that affect cyberspace
operations certification.
         (g) Support cyberspace operations team recertification processes and events through
technical input, guidance, and task execution.
     (3) CW4 must--
         (a) Perform duties described in paragraph g (2).
         (b) Evaluate cyber defense requirements and advise in the joint targeting process.
         (c) Provide subject matter expert advice, planning, coordination across echelon, and task
execution within cyberspace operations.
         (d) Provide cyber operations recommendations and guidance on Army, Coalition, and
National policies, structures, assignments and training.
         (e) Supervise military, civilian, and joint/coalition personnel throughout the planning,
coordination, and execution of cyberspace operations.
    (4) CW5 must--
         (a) Perform duties described in paragraph g (3).
         (b) Advise the commander, leaders, and other forums regarding cyberspace operations,
risk mitigation, friendly/threat capabilities, policies, authorities, and employment strategies across
all echelons.
         (c) Provide input regarding the readiness of cyberspace operational organizations, teams,
personnel, infrastructure, and capabilities.
         (d) Coordinate with service schools to identify mitigation strategies for knowledge and skill
gaps to reduce operational training requirements.
         (e) Provide guidance, mentorship, and direction to junior Warrant Officers within the
command or organization.
          f) Direct mission management functions for offensive and defensive cyberspace
operations.
         ( g) Develop crisis plans to directly support cyberspace operations planning and targeting.
h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
         (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
         (2) Meet medical and physical standards per AR 40-501.

       (3) Table 8-170A-1. Physical requirements - A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long
Jump (LJ) – 0120 cm, seated Power Throw (PT) – 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs.,
and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0036 shuttles.
       (4) Authorized position titles are provided in appendixes B and C. The following grades are
used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels: W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals
 CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed in the following standards of
grade tables:
            (a) Table 8-170A-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE (Not Applicable)
            (b) Table 8-170A-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
